the Sentinel 1 data can be used to monitor surface deformation with millimeter accuracy, provided that an atmospheric correction model is available, and that a reference point, close to the target, is known with millimeter accuracy.

the Sentinel 1 mission will provide a new opportunity to perform millimeter precision InSAR analysis over the entire planet, with an unprecedented frequency of observations and a high level of reliability.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the most accurate InSAR analysis techniques for the Sentinel 1 mission and the evaluation of the expected precision of the measurements.

the development of new algorithms for InSAR data processing and analysis, in order to improve the quality of the displacement measurements, to reduce the computational cost, to increase the spatial density of the measurements and to reduce the time required to produce results from the data.

the development of a methodology for the analysis of SAR interferometric data from Sentinel 1 and the other X band satellites, to provide a millimeter level accuracy in the measurement of surface deformation, in the case of a short time series of images.

the new Sentinel 1 satellite mission will provide a significant improvement in the precision of ground motion measurements, thanks to its high revisit time and its global coverage.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the precision achievable with Sentinel 1 data, for a given target and observation time frame, is comparable to the one achieved with Cosmo Skymede data.
the Sentinel 1 mission is a key factor for the success of InSAR techniques in geophysical inversion.
the Sentinel 1 data, with a revisit time of a few days, will be a powerful tool for geophysical inversion and for monitoring and risk management.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the accuracy of Sentinel 1 data can be improved by a factor of 3, with respect to the current state of the art, by applying the new interferometric processing techniques developed for the COSMO Skymed mission (De Zan et al 2008, De Zan and Guarnieri 2007) and using an accurate model of water vapor.
Sentinel 1 will provide a unique opportunity to monitor ground deformation phenomena with unprecedented accuracy and frequency and to use the data for the inversion of geophysical models.
the Sentinel 1 mission will be an excellent tool to measure surface displacements with millimeter accuracy over a wide area, at sub weekly frequency, with a very short turnaround time.
